newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, Hanbo probe no big factor.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, Hanbo probe no big factor.

text.p: Shares closed higher on Monday led by blue chips which attracted investors ahead of the planned rise in foreign stock ownership ceilings in May, brokers said.
They said POSCO and Samsung Electronics spearheaded the blue chip gains.
The composite stock index ended at 694.90, up 7.48 points.
"Institutions snapped up blue chips ahead of the ceiling expansion in May," said Park Ki-pyong of Hangynag Securities.
The testimony of the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group in a parliamentary hearing on the conglomerate's collapse in January had no major impact on the market, brokers said.
"The Hanbo founder is saying nothing substantial to affect the market," Park said. But he said investors would pay attention to the hearing over the loans-for-kickback scandal.
POSCO gained 1,500 won to 53,800 and Samsung Electronics rose 1,800 won to 63,800.
Brokers said investors pinned their hopes for an economic turnaround on the back of rebounding prices of steel goods, semiconductors and petrochmeical products.
"Anticipation of improving economic fundamentals greatly contributed to stabilising market sentiment," said Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland.

Brokers said construction shares were in demand aided by investors' optimism that four-way peace talks could promote inter-Korean economic cooperation. North Korea has asked for a second briefing with South Korea and the U.S. on proposed peace talks. The construction sub-index rose 3.83 percent to 280.03.

Brokers said the shares also rose on news reports, denied by a party official, that the ruling New Korea Party was considering allowing the issuance of long-term bonds to anonymous purchasers to lure underground money into infrastructure construction.
Brokers forecast a downward correction after the index touches the 720 level. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
